## Why excaliplant?

- **Looks like a whiteboard, stays a diagram.** Output is a real Excalidraw scene: open it in Excalidraw, move boxes, arrows stay bound.
- **Broad PlantUML coverage.** Sequence, class, activity, state, component, C4, Gantt, mind maps, JSON, regex, math — see the [full list](#supported-diagrams).
- **The PlantUML language, not just diagrams.** Preprocessor (`!procedure`, `!function`, loops, JSON variables, `!include`), Creole markup, `skinparam`, `<style>`, themes, colours and bundled C4/ArchiMate libraries.
- **Pure JavaScript.** No Java, no Graphviz, no PlantUML server. Layout runs on [ELK](https://github.com/kieler/elkjs) and purpose-built engines.
- **Deterministic.** Same input, same bytes — ideal for docs in git.
- **Safe for untrusted input.** Resource limits, escaped output, no file or network access unless you opt in.

## Quick start

```sh
npm install @grethel-labs/excaliplant
```

### Command line

```sh
npx excaliplant diagram.puml -o diagram.svg          # hand-drawn SVG
npx excaliplant diagram.puml -o diagram.png --width 1600
npx excaliplant diagram.puml -o diagram.excalidraw   # open in excalidraw.com
cat diagram.puml | npx excaliplant -f svg --theme dark > diagram.svg
```

### JavaScript

```js
import { render } from "@grethel-labs/excaliplant";

const result = await render(`
@startuml
Alice -> Bob : hello
Bob --> Alice : hi!
@enduml
`);

result.kind; //           "sequence"
result.excalidraw; //     Excalidraw scene (JSON)
await result.toSvg(); //  standalone SVG with embedded Excalifont
await result.toPng({ width: 1200 }); // PNG Buffer
result.diagnostics; //    warnings with line numbers
```

## How it works

<img src="docs/assets/pipeline.png" alt="excaliplant pipeline" />

Each diagram type is a small module with four hooks — `detect`, `parse`, `layout`, `draw` — on top of a shared core (preprocessor, PlantUML syntax helpers, text measurement with real font metrics, a drawing canvas and the renderers). Modules never touch Excalidraw or SVG directly; they draw shapes on a canvas, which keeps the three output formats in sync. See [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## PlantUML language support

| Feature          | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Preprocessor     | `!$var`, `!define`/`!definelong`, `!if`/`!elseif`/`!else`, `!ifdef`, `!while`, `!foreach`, `!procedure`, `!function`/`!return`, default and keyword arguments, JSON variables, builtins (`%strlen`, `%upper`, `%date`, `%lighten`, …), `!include`/`!includesub` via resolver, `!theme`, `!pragma`, `!log`, `!assert` |
| Standard library | Bundled, offline implementations of `<C4/C4_Context>`, `<C4/C4_Container>`, `<C4/C4_Component>`, … and `<archimate/Archimate>`                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Creole           | `**bold**`, `//italic//`, `""mono""`, `--strike--`, `__underline__`, `~~wave~~`, headings, bullet and numbered lists, tables, separators, `<b>`, `<i>`, `<color>`, `<size>`, `<back>`, `<sub>`, `<sup>`, `[[links]]`, `<U+XXXX>`                                                                                     |
| Styling          | `skinparam` (single line and blocks), `<style>` sheets, inline colours `#back;line:red;line.dashed;text:blue`, all HTML colour names, gradients (first colour)                                                                                                                                                       |
| Commons          | `title`, `caption`, `header`, `footer`, `legend`, `mainframe`, `hide`/`show`, `left to right direction`, `newpage`, multiple `@start…@end` blocks                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Themes

Pick a theme with `--theme` / `{ theme }`, or let PlantUML's `!theme` choose the closest match. Available: {{themes}}. Add `--clean` / `{ sketch: false }` for straight lines.

{{themeGrid}}

## API

| Export                                    | Description                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `render(source, options?)`                | Render the first (or `options.block`) diagram → `RenderResult`    |
| `renderAll(source, options?)`             | Render every `@start…@end` block                                  |
| `parse(source, options?)`                 | Parse without layout → `{ kind, model, diagnostics }`             |
| `detectKind(source)`                      | Detected diagram kind                                             |
| `listDiagramTypes()`                      | Supported kinds and their start keywords                          |
| `renderPlantUml(source)`                  | 0.x-compatible: `await` → Excalidraw JSON, `.toSvg()`, `.toPng()` |
| `preprocessText(source, options?)`        | Run only the preprocessor                                         |
| `DiagramRegistry`, `defineDiagram`        | Register your own diagram modules                                 |
| `THEMES`, `THEME_NAMES`, `DEFAULT_LIMITS` | Built-in themes and resource limits                               |

`RenderResult` has `kind`, `name`, `excalidraw`, `diagnostics`, `pages`, `model`, `toJSON()`, `toSvg({ padding, background, embedFont })` and `toPng({ width, scale, background })`.

<details>
<summary><b>Render options</b></summary>

| Option     | Default          | Description                                                               |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme`    | `"sketch"`       | Theme name or theme object                                                |
| `sketch`   | theme default    | `false` for clean strokes                                                 |
| `seed`     | `"excaliplant"`  | Seed for ids and stroke wobble                                            |
| `block`    | `0`              | Block index or `@startuml name`                                           |
| `page`     | `0`              | Page of a `newpage` document                                              |
| `strict`   | `false`          | Throw on unrecognised lines instead of warning                            |
| `include`  | —                | `(target, { from, kind }) => string \| null` resolver for `!include`      |
| `defines`  | —                | Predefined preprocessor variables                                         |
| `date`     | `null`           | Date returned by `%date()` (empty by default for reproducible output)     |
| `limits`   | `DEFAULT_LIMITS` | Input size, lines, nodes, edges, elements, preprocessor budget, PNG width |
| `kind`     | auto             | Force a diagram module                                                    |
| `registry` | built-in         | Custom `DiagramRegistry`                                                  |

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>CLI options</b></summary>

```text
excaliplant [input.puml] [-o output] [options]

  -o, --output <file>       Output file (format from extension unless -f is given)
  -f, --format <fmt>        excalidraw | svg | png
  -t, --theme <name>        sketch | plain | hachure | mono | dark | blueprint
      --clean               Clean strokes instead of the hand-drawn look
      --width <px>          PNG width (16–16000)
      --scale <n>           PNG scale relative to the SVG size (default 2)
      --background <color>  Background colour for SVG/PNG
      --seed <value>        Seed for stroke wobble and element ids
      --page <n>            Page of a newpage document
      --all                 Render every block ("{n}" in -o is the block number)
      --include-dir <dir>   Allow !include of files below <dir>
  -D, --define NAME=value   Predefine a preprocessor variable
      --strict              Fail on unrecognised lines
      --list-types          List supported diagram types
```

</details>

## Security

excaliplant is built to render untrusted PlantUML:

- No file-system or network access while rendering. `!include` only works through a resolver you pass in (the CLI's `--include-dir` restricts includes to one directory tree); `!includeurl` and `!import` are refused.
- Every text and attribute in SVG output is escaped; colours are validated; links are limited to `http(s)` and `mailto`.
- Budgets for input size, lines, preprocessor steps/recursion/loop iterations, nodes, edges, drawing elements and PNG size (see `DEFAULT_LIMITS`).
- Parsers are scanner-based or use bounded regular expressions; hostile inputs are covered by [`test/security.test.mjs`](test/security.test.mjs).

Please report vulnerabilities as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Compatibility notes

excaliplant re-implements PlantUML in JavaScript, so diagrams look different from PlantUML's output — that is the point. Layout decisions differ (ELK instead of Graphviz), sprites and `<&icons>` render as placeholder glyphs, and the bundled standard library covers C4 and ArchiMate only. Unknown lines are reported as warnings (or errors with `strict`), never silently dropped.

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm test            # node:test suite (examples, syntax, security, CLI)
npm run typecheck   # tsc --checkJs
npm run format      # prettier
npm run docs        # regenerate gallery, screenshots and this README
npm run check       # everything CI checks
```

Add a diagram example by dropping a `.puml` file into `examples/<kind>/` — it becomes a test case and a gallery entry. Contribution guidelines live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Releases are fully automated: every pull request carries one `release:major|minor|patch|none` label, and merging publishes the next version to npm with provenance (see [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md)).
